failures.title: FRAME trend series had no scheduled writer
failures.evidence: append_trend() is called only inside the GET /frame/probe handler (main.py:113). No systemd timer, no crontab entry, and no internal scheduler referenced that endpoint. Series held 21 points across 22 days in an irregular pattern (4,1,2,1,1,1,6,2,3) — the signature of manual invocation.
failures.impact: FRAME's trend/drift chambers produced no continuity; an observer with no heartbeat degrades to cosmetic
failures.repair: frame-probe.service + frame-probe.timer installed (OnBootSec=3m, OnUnitActiveSec=15m); series 22 -> 24 lines, 3 points in the 30 min after install

failures.title: Two sessions mutated the observability plane inside nine minutes with no lock, claim, or announcement
failures.evidence: This audit measured :18902/health as connection-refused at 13:35 (+08) and recorded the absence as a Phase 2 blocker. At 13:41:48 a different session created /root/scripts/kabarkan_health_server.py, installed and started kabarkan-health.service, and added 'kabarkan: 18902' to FRAME's live ORGAN_PORTS. By 13:42:13 FRAME reported organs_up=10/10. This audit's receipt was invalidated on its central claim within nine minutes of being written.
failures.impact: Two sessions each believed they acted on current state; one was already stale. Any audit artifact written during a window of unsynchronised writes can be falsified after it is written and before it is read. This is the mechanism, not an accident: multi-session infra writes take no lock, so correctness depends on sweeping ALL sessions by timestamp before any claim of current state.
failures.recommended_action: before asserting state in a shared report, sweep files newer than the audit start (find -newermt) across /root/scripts, /etc/systemd/system and the target repo; stamp every artifact with its measurement window and record post-window changes as explicit addenda rather than silent rewrites

failures.title: An existing kabarkan-observability skill documents the plane and was not consulted before the audit
failures.evidence: /root/.hermes/skills/domains/general/forge/telemetry/kabarkan-observability/SKILL.md (18,054 B, mtime 2026-09-14) documents the pipeline, the canonical subject pattern kabarkan.ingest.span.{trace_id}, the Langfuse backends (cloud jp.cloud.langfuse.com quota-exhausted; self-host localhost:4000, 0 traces), and the ObservationRecord model. It was found only in a second pass after a filesystem sweep.
failures.impact: Three artifacts were written without it: the dependency graph missed the metrics publisher (kabarkan-publish.py), the vector receipt proposed a contract that already exists upstream in arifFlow/spec/KABARKAN_FQ_INSTRUMENTATION.md, and the config reconstruction used cloud.langfuse.com where the documented endpoints were jp.cloud.langfuse.com or localhost:4000. The skill is itself stale (dated 2026-07-24, describes 240 rows against today's 201,554) but remains the authoritative operational reference.
failures.recommended_action: load the domain skill before probing a subsystem that has one; refresh the skill's 'Current State' block
